origin.description: Extract one inclusive code-point range from each string.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A character vector, or another vector that can be coerced to character.

arguments.name: start, end
arguments.text: Inclusive code-point positions. Positive values count from the left, starting at 1, and negative values count from the right. start may instead be a two-column matrix named start/end or start/length.

origin.details: string, start, and end must share a size: length 1 recycles, and any other mismatch is an error. When start is a matrix, end is size-checked and not passed to the extractor. Names are kept only when string is not recycled. A range that ends before it starts, or that starts past the string, is empty.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as the recycled inputs.
origin.example:
hw <- "Hadley Wickham"
cat(paste0("str_sub(hw, 1, 6) returns ", str_sub(hw, 1, 6), ".\n"))
cat(paste0("str_sub(hw, -7) returns ", str_sub(hw, -7), ".\n"))
cat(paste0("str_sub(hw, c(1, 8), c(6, 14)) returns ", paste(str_sub(hw, c(1, 8), c(6, 14)), collapse = ", "), ".\n"))

translation.description: Check sizes with size_common, then extract with stringi.stri_sub.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: start
arguments.text: A start position, a list of positions, a list of rows, an IndexMatrix, or a dict with two columns.

arguments.name: end
arguments.text: An inclusive end. Ignored when start is a matrix, aside from the size check. The default is -1.

translation.details: A dict whose second key is length uses a width instead of an end. A list of rows is a matrix for this function. Names are copied only when the result has the same length as string. The result is a list.
translation.value: A list of strings. A missing string or a missing index is NA. An empty range is an empty string.
translation.example:
from stringr.sub import str_sub
hw = "Hadley Wickham"
print("str_sub(hw, 1, 6) returns " + str_sub(hw, 1, 6)[0] + ".")
print("str_sub(hw, -7) returns " + str_sub(hw, -7)[0] + ".")
print("str_sub(hw, c(1, 8), c(6, 14)) returns " + ", ".join(str_sub(hw, [1, 8], [6, 14])) + ".")
